parameters.query:
-- One contact per company, verified valid, company not blocked and not
-- already in a live thread.
--
-- `sources` is comma-separated multi-value, so match per element -- never
-- with = on the whole field, which silently drops rows carrying two tags.
--
-- Two independent guards, both on outreach_log rather than on a flag, so a
-- run that crashes halfway can be restarted without mailing anyone twice:
--   * offer-level -- a company that already got THIS offer_id can never be
--                    picked again;
--   * MODE        -- who is eligible at all.
--       new    = no outreach_log row at all, in any campaign. The first
--                send to a list: these firms have never been written to.
--       repeat = already touched in this campaign, and the last touch is at
--                least MIN_DAYS_SINCE_LAST days old.
--
-- SENDER SPLIT. The final select alternates A / B over a randomly ordered
-- batch. That gives an exactly even split of volume between the two
-- mailboxes and a random pairing of company to sender -- a plain coin flip
-- per row would drift 10-20 either way over a batch of 300, which matters
-- because each mailbox has its own sending reputation and quota.
-- The assignment is made once, here, and travels with the row, so the same
-- company is greeted, sent and logged under one sender.
with candidates as (
  select distinct on (co.company_key)
         c.id as contact_id,
         c.email,
         co.company_key,
         co.company_name,
         co.country,
         not exists (
           select 1 from outreach_log o where o.company_key = co.company_key
         ) as is_first_touch
    from contacts c
    join companies co on co.company_key = c.company_key
   where exists (
           select 1 from unnest(string_to_array(c.sources, ',')) s
            where trim(s) = '{{ $('Run settings').first().json.source }}'
         )
     and (not {{ $('Run settings').first().json.only_this_source }}::boolean
          or array_length(string_to_array(co.sources, ','), 1) = 1)
     and c.verification_status = 'valid'
     and c.email_status is distinct from 'bounced'
     and co.contact_status is null
     and not exists (
           select 1 from outreach_log o
            where o.company_key = co.company_key
              and o.campaign    = '{{ $('Run settings').first().json.campaign }}'
              and o.notes       = 'offer:{{ $('Run settings').first().json.offer_id }}'
         )
     and (
       ('{{ $('Run settings').first().json.mode }}' = 'new' and not exists (
            select 1 from outreach_log o where o.company_key = co.company_key))
       or
       ('{{ $('Run settings').first().json.mode }}' = 'repeat' and exists (
            select 1 from outreach_log o
             where o.company_key = co.company_key
               and o.campaign    = '{{ $('Run settings').first().json.campaign }}')
        and (select max(o.event_date) from outreach_log o
              where o.company_key = co.company_key
                and o.campaign    = '{{ $('Run settings').first().json.campaign }}')
            <= current_date - {{ $('Run settings').first().json.min_days }})
     )
   order by co.company_key, c.id
),
picked as (
  select * from candidates order by random() limit {{ $('Run settings').first().json.batch }}
)
select p.*,
       case when row_number() over (order by random()) % 2 = 0 then 'A' else 'B' end as who
  from picked p;

parameters.content:
## Offer send, straight from Postgres

Set everything in **Run settings**, then Execute.

- one address per company, verified valid only
- **Select companies** splits the batch evenly between sender A and sender B at random
- the re-send guard is `outreach_log`, not a flag, so a crashed run can be restarted without mailing anyone twice
- offer text lives in the `offers` table, keyed by `offer_id`
- for a follow-up offer: new `OFFER_ID`, `MODE = 'repeat'`, `BATCH` = the size of the list. Bounced and blocked companies drop out on their own.
